data.narrative:
Kairos Power is a late-stage nuclear energy developer founded by Mike Laufer, Edward Blandford, and Per Peterson that has raised $500M+. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 8 comparable companies—3 publicly traded (Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, NuScale) and 5 private peers (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, TerraPower)—though narrow peer matching proved limited.

A Stage-Progression methodology was applied, using the $500M total capital raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.2x multiplier typical of Late Stage to next-stage transitions. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $600M. A Peer-Median triangulation was not applicable; while four same-sector peers exist, none met narrow stage and tier filters (requiring ≥3 datapoints), making sector-wide median comparison unreliable and potentially misleading given the heterogeneity of nuclear technology platforms.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $510M–$690M, with a median point estimate of $600M. This range reflects the stage-appropriate step-up from deployed capital while acknowledging material uncertainty around comparable company selection in a nascent, heterogeneous sector. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage nuclear peers with disclosed valuations and differentiation in technology risk across the competitive set.
